Tai-Ilara

Overview

Tai-Ilara is the woman Kir remembers from his childhood on Jigran. After he rescues her, she asks him to retrieve her belongings. Kel dies during that expedition, and Tai-Ilara’s dismissive response destroys Kir’s idealised image of his old attachment. Her part in the story reveals what Kir had failed to recognise in Kel. [1, 2, 3]

The freed Joons and Kir’s family

Kel and Rad discover that Firez is moving the Joon prisoners from the mountain prison into his fortress. Kel plans an attack on the transfer, avoiding a direct prison assault. Among those freed are Tai-Ilara, whom Kir admired as a child, and the elder Tui-Len. Tai-Ilara welcomes his changed appearance and asks him to retrieve belongings left behind. Tui-Len brings harder news: Kir’s parents are dead. The elder fears that killing Firez will expose the survivors to the Curse, but Kir tells him that Tka-Rik and At-Zako have already destroyed it. Tui-Len also opens the sealed Joon cache whose amulet Kir has recovered. [4, 1, 5, 6, 7, 8]

Tai-Ilara’s request and Kel’s death

Seeing Kir reunited with Tai-Ilara, Kel asks for the way back to Suslanger. Kir begs her to stay and mentions one more expedition for Tai-Ilara’s belongings. Kel agrees because she still fears for him, calling it their last adventure together. She dies during that expedition. On Kir’s return, Tai-Ilara is concerned with her comb and mirror and dismisses his grief. Her reaction breaks his idealised childhood attachment. He recognises Kel as the person who was closest and most loyal to him, and realises that he failed to see her love while she was beside him. [2, 3, 9]
